message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
You can use either:

* the `gcloud` CLI (recommended for quick testing), or  
* the REST API (useful if you’re building a programmatic deployment).

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`).  
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled for that project.  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have a service account key if you’re calling the REST API directly.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: add a startup script
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What this does

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk (adjust as needed). |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you want to install the NVIDIA driver automatically, add a `startup.sh` script that runs the driver installer. Google’s Compute Engine documentation has a ready‑made script you can copy.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the REST API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline or a custom tool), here’s the exact JSON payload you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
The `startup-script` is optional but recommended to install the NVIDIA driver automatically.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="get(status, statusMessage)"
```

You should see `RUNNING` and no error messages.  
SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project="$PROJECT_ID" --zone="$ZONE"
$ nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Summary

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ...` – easiest for interactive use.  
* **REST**: POST to `/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances` with the JSON body above – great for automation.  

Both approaches will give you a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
